aged 8 years and studying in 4th standard.
On 16.11.2019, the Informant left her house for work and returned in the evening at 06.00 p.m.
She found the Victim in a scared and frightened condition.
On enquiry with the Victim, the Victim informed her that, on 12.11.2019 in the afternoon while she was watching Television (TV) at her home, the Appellant came in the hall and slept on the cot.
The Appellant opened the zip of his pant and gave his penis in her mouth and left the house.
Thereafter on 13.11.2019 when the Victim returned from the school in the evening, the Appellant again came at her house and did the same act with the Victim.
As 4 apeal774.2023.odt the Victim was afraid of her mother, she did not inform immediately about the said acts of the Appellant.
The Victim informed her aunt about the said acts of the Appellant.
The Informant informed her brother who was residing in different district.
After discussion, the Report was lodged.

a) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, the relations between the Informant and the Appellant were not cordial.
There are omissions in the testimony of the Victim.
No witness was examined in support of the Birth Certificate brought on record.
The age of the Victim was not proved.
There was no dispute in respect of the spot.
Though the Victim's aunt came to know about the incident, she kept mum.
The medical evidence do not corroborate the Victim's testimony.
There was delay in lodging the Report with the Police.
The Charge was not conclusively proved and, therefore, the Appellant was entitled for acquittal.
b) It is submitted by the learned A.P.P. that, no suggestion was given to the Informant that, there was dispute between both the sides.
Victim denied the suggestions in the cross-examination.
The omissions are not proved through the Investigating Officer.
The testimony of the mother and the aunt of the Victim supports the Victim's version.
The Birth Certificate was exhibited.
The medical history corroborates the Victim's version.
Witness No.8 saw the Appellant fleeing from Victim's house.
There are no suggestions that, the Victim was major.
Except denial, nothing has come on record to show that, the Appellant was falsely implicated.
As the foundational facts were proved, the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act comes into 7 apeal774.2023.odt play.
There was no merit in the Appeal and the same be dismissed.
c) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Victim that, she adopts the submissions made by the learned A.P.P.
The learned trial Court has rightly appreciated the evidence on record and the Appeal be dismissed.

4. To prove that, the Victim was a 'child' as defined under Section 2(d) of the POCSO Act i.e. below 18 years of age, the prosecution relied on the testimony of the Informant who is the mother of Victim and the Birth Certificate.
The evidence of P.W.2 Informant shows that, she was mother of Victim.
There is no dispute on this aspect.

Though initially in her examination-in-chief she deposed that, the date of birth of the Victim was 20.04.2001, she was recalled and in her further examination-in-chief she deposed that, the date of birth of Victim was 21.04.2011.

She deposed that,
the earlier date of birth was wrongly mentioned.
The cross-examination of this Informant shows that, the age of the Victim was not seriously disputed.
In the evidence of this Informant, the Birth Certificate below Exh.45 is brought on record.
Her evidence shows that, she brought the original Birth Certificate and on verifying by the learned trial Court, the copy is taken on record below Exh.45.
Suggestion that, false certificate was filed is denied.
The said Exh.45 is the Birth 8 apeal774.2023.odt Certificate issued by the concerned Municipal Council.
The date of issue was 24.03.2014 i.e. much prior to the lodging of the F.I.R.

As nothing has come in the cross-examination to create any doubt about the authenticity of said public document and as there is no serious challenge to the date of birth and the age of Victim, it can be conveniently said that, the prosecution established that, the Victim was the 'child' at the time of lodging the F.I.R.
5.
The undisputed aspect of the matter is that, the Appellant was known to the Victim and her mother, as they are the resident of the same locality.
The case of the prosecution is that of oral sexual assault on the Victim by the Appellant i.e. giving penis in the mouth of the Victim.
The Victim's testimony is crucial.
In her evidence Victim deposed that, on 12th and 13th when she was present in her house, the Appellant came, opened zip of his pant and gave his penis into her mouth.

sentences.text: 4 The Victim informed about the said act to P.W.4 aunt of the Victim.
Her aunt tried to apprehend the Appellant, but in vain.
She informed the incident to her mother and the Report was lodged.
The cross-examination of the Victim shows that, her house comprised of two rooms.
The house of the Victim which was the place of incident, was exactly adjacent to the road.

It has come in the Victim's cross-examination that, the road in front of the house was busy 9 apeal774.2023.odt road, the cot was in the first room, the entrance door of the house was big and the cot was visible from the door.
In the cross-examination of P.W.3 Spot-Panch it has come on record that, the spot of incident was adjacent to the road which was busy road and the door of the house was big.
The Spot-Panchanama below Exh.34, corroborates the said evidence in respect of the spot of incident.
From this evidence on record, it is clear that, the spot of incident was not the secluded place.
It is not the evidence of the Victim that, the door of the house was closed at the time of incident.

If this is the evidence on record,
it appears improbable that, the said act of sexual assault will be committed on the cot in the first room of the house in the day time, which was visible from the door.
6. The evidence of the Victim shows that, she was afraid of her mother.
Even the evidence of Victim's mother shows that, the Victim was very frightened of her.
Even the evidence of P.W.4 aunt of the Victim corroborates the said version that, the Victim was afraid of her mother.
Suggestions of tutoring are given to the Victim and her mother in the cross-examination.
Undisputedly, there is six (6) days delay in lodging the Report.

The Appellant in the cross-examination of the Informant, who is the mother of Victim, elicited the reason for the delay that, she was alone and she called her elder brother (P.W.6) and after he came, they 10 apeal774.2023.odt discussed the matter and lodged the Report.

Even though the aspect of delay itself will not be fatal for the prosecution, it is brought in the evidence of the Victim and the evidence of P.W.6 maternal uncle of the Victim that, relations between the Informant i.e. mother of the Victim and the Appellant were not cordial.
The Victim in her cross-examination admitted that, sometimes quarrel used to take place between her mother and the Appellant.
P.W.6 Laxman Kamble in his cross-examination admitted that, on account of compound wall of the house, the Appellant used to trouble the Informant.
From this evidence on record, the Appellant has successfully brought on record the strained relations between the Informant and the Appellant.
However, the Victim's mother denied that, the quarrel had taken place between her and the Appellant.
This indicates that, the Informant cannot be called a witness of truth.

7. Though P.W.4 Vaishali Lambat, the aunt of Victim, in her evidence deposed that, she was informed by the Victim about the incident and she asked the Appellant about the incident and the Appellant fled, she did not lodge the report.
However, later on i.e. after crime was registered, this P.W.4 Vaishali Lambat herself went to the police for giving statement.
Her evidence shows that, she was graduate in Arts and residing in the same locality where the 11 apeal774.2023.odt incident took place.
Thus, her inaction makes her testimony fragile.
8. The evidence of P.W.7 Monika Aakre shows that, she was the Professor in Gynecology in the Government Medical College Nagpur.
She examined the Victim who was brought by the Lady Police Constable.
She found no internal or external injuries on the Victim.
The Victim's hymen was intact.
She took the samples of the Victim for sending it to the Chemical Analyzer.

Though she deposed that, in her opinion, possibility of sexual violence cannot be ruled out, there is no supportive Ravindra Kashinath Nandanwar vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Khapa ... on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81857053/
5 material to corroborate her said evidence.

sentences.text: The Medico Legal Examination Report of the Victim is brought on record below Exh.74.
The para No.25 in respect of final opinion ( after receiving lab reports), is not supported by the reports of the Chemical Analyzer.
The blank space in the said para is in respect of laboratory report.

The said para 25 is reproduced below:-
"25. Final Opinion (After receiving Lab reports) Findings in support of the above opinion, taking into account the history, clinical examination findings and Laboratory reports of ......................... bearing identification marks described above,
...................... hours/ days after the incident of sexual violence

, I am of the opinion that:
As the survivor was examined after 1 week of the stated incidence & considering her history and clinical examination (No c/o any injuries) - sexual violence cannot be ruled out.
 12 apeal774.2023.odt  Signature of Examining Doctor Sd/-
 Name of Examining Doctor Dr. Monika Akare,
 Seal Assistant Prof. Dept. of  IGGMCH, Nagpur Place : IGGMCH, Nagpur"
The above discussed medical evidence do not take the case of prosecution any further in establishing the Charge.
9.
The above discussed evidence on record shows that, the Victim was afraid of her mother.
Relations between the Victim's mother and the Appellant were strained.
The Victim's mother denied the strained relations which indicates that, she cannot be relied.

The spot of incident was such that,
it is improbable that, the said act as deposed by the Victim was committed.

The Victim's version,
therefore, in respect of sexual assault by the Appellant on her is required to be seen with doubt.

The Appellant in his statement under Section 313(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure stated that,
the quarrel took place between him and the Victim's mother and, therefore, he was falsely implicated.

Though it can be said that, no one will register the case with such allegations, to raise presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, the prosecution has to establish the foundational facts of the case.
As discussed above, the foundational facts of the case itself appear to be doubtful.
The Appellant rebutted the presumption by bringing on record the possibility of false implication.
Under these facts and 13 apeal774.2023.odt circumstances of the case, the Appellant is entitled for benefit of doubt and resultantly for acquittal.
Hence, the following order:-

ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed.
